title: Syntology paper-to-implementation benchmark: published artifact shapes
description: The four shapes a machine reading this repository has to understand, in one file so there are no cross-file $refs to resolve. Point a validator at '#/$defs/<name>'. tools/validate_schemas.py validates every shipped artifact against these on every push (.github/workflows/ci.yml), so this file is a checked contract rather than documentation of one. What a schema CANNOT tell you is in README.md, 'What is NOT claimed': `passed` is a property-suite outcome, not a correctness claim, and `served_level` is what execution checks a sample passed, never fidelity to the paper.

provenance.title: syntology-provenance/1
provenance.description: STANDARDS.md R1: every derived artifact records what it was derived from. Internal paths appear as stable aliases (<BENCH>, <REFIMPL>, <AUDIT>, <INTERNAL>, <CORPUS>, <REPO>, <HOME>) -- see ASSEMBLY_REPORT.md 1.

inputs.description: Each input with its sha256 at read time.

task.title: One benchmark task
task.description: A row of tasks/*.json['tasks']. The subject is given method, paper, entry, signature and first_sentence -- and nothing else. Deriving the rest of the contract is the work the retrieval arms exist for.

task_id.description: Prefix encodes the stratum this task was drawn into: in__ = in-catalog, off_ = off-catalog, sub_ = substitution-set.

stratum.description: in_catalog tasks are the ones where the graph already served a verified implementation, so fetch-and-submit passes by construction -- README.md says why that asymmetry is the mechanism under test and not a flaw.

served_level.description: V0-V4 execution-verification level of the implementation the graph would serve, or -1 for a task with no served implementation at draw time (34 of the 120 task rows, in both strata). NOT a fidelity claim: the audit behind data/fidelity_audit/ found the ladder buys no fidelity.

entry.description: The function the submission must define.

first_sentence.description: The ONLY specification text the subject receives.

pass_both.description: A run passes iff every property named here passes, checked with `is True`.

suspect_tests.description: Properties the drafter is known to have got wrong. Excluded from pass_both and ignored.

run_meta.title: One run's structure: data/runs/<sweep>/<task_id>/<arm>/meta.json
run_meta.description: What happened, with nothing that was retrieved. Every tool call by NAME and argument SIZE; the bodies live only in the redacted transcript beside it as sha256 digests.

arm.description: _ho = the hold-out variant, where the answer was removed from the arm's reach.

base_arm.description: Present on hold-out-sweep runs: the arm this one is the hold-out form of. The floor arm carries base_arm `none` -- there is nothing to hold out from it, and it is in the sweep as the comparison.

model_id.description: One subject model throughout: Claude Sonnet 4.5 on Bedrock.

variant.description: Pins the tool descriptions and MCP server instructions. Absent or explicitly null on run 1, which predates the pin (96 runs omit it, 24 record null); v14_freeze from the freeze onward. Adoption moves with this string -- 0/24 vs 18/24 on the same tools.

stop_reason.description: tool_use = the 20-turn cap was reached with no submission.

holdout_shas.description: The code samples this run was DENIED. Present on hold-out-sweep runs; src/verify_holdout.py audits that none of them was reachable. TWO SPELLINGS, measured: the v16 hold-out arms record a 16-hex PREFIX (400 entries) and the rest record the full 64-hex sha256 (114). Match on the prefix if you are joining these to a code_sha256.

result_row.title: One referee verdict: a row of data/results*.json['runs']
result_row.description: The referee is deterministic, local, blind to the arms and identical across every run. `passed` means every property in the task's pass_both set returned True. It is NOT a claim that the module implements the paper -- README.md, 'What is NOT claimed', point 3.

properties_required.description: len(pass_both). Absent when there was nothing to score.

reason.description: Why there is no property outcome. no_submission = the agent hit the turn cap; the search arm did this in 11 of 24 freeze runs.

manifest.title: MANIFEST.json
manifest.description: Every file in this repository, its sha256, and the internal artifact it came from. tools/check_clean_clone.py verifies a clone against it with no credentials; tools/assemble.py --check additionally re-derives it from the working repo, which only the publisher can do.

problems.description: Non-empty means the assembler found something wrong and said so. A published tree has none.

source.description: Where this file came from, with internal directory names replaced by stable aliases.

rule.description: How it got here. `verbatim` = byte-identical to the code that produced the numbers; `portability-patched` = one of the 18 files with a listed, non-behavioural path fix (src/PORTABILITY_PATCHES.md).
